title: How to Plan a Women's Trip to Namibia, From Dune Sunrises to Desert Elephants
meta_title: Women's Trip to Namibia: Route, Safety and Group Costs
meta_description: Plan a women's trip to Namibia with friends: a 10-day route, real park and visa fees, safety advice and how group pricing works. Get a free group quote.
excerpt: A women's trip to Namibia works best as a private, guided loop through Sossusvlei, Swakopmund, Damaraland and Etosha. Here is the route, the fees, safety advice and how group payments work.
content:
A women's trip to Namibia works best as a private, guided road trip of 8 to 12 days that links the red dunes of Sossusvlei, the desert elephants of Damaraland, the coast at Swakopmund and the waterholes of Etosha. Plan for two nights per stop, one shared vehicle and the dry months of May to October.

Getting a group of friends, sisters or club members to agree on dates is hard enough. Then come the long gravel drives, rooming, budgets and a few worries about safety. This guide lays out a route, real fees, safety advice and how the money works when everyone pays her own share, so you can plan our special occasion and group safaris with confidence.

Quick Facts

  • Ideal length: 8 to 12 days, with two nights at each stop
  • Best months: May to October (dry, cool nights, best Etosha waterholes)
  • Group size: 4 to 7 fits one 4x4; 8 to 14 suits a larger safari vehicle
  • Park fees: N$280 per foreign adult per entry to parks like Etosha and Namib-Naukluft (checked November 2026)
  • Visa for UK visitors: N$1,600 per adult, on arrival or as an e-visa (checked November 2026)
  • Group perk: Every seventh place is free for every six paying travellers

Why Does Namibia Suit a Women's Group?

Namibia suits a women's group because it offers big landscapes, low crowds and a slow, sociable pace. The country has about three million people spread across more than 820,000 km², so days are spent in wide open spaces, and evenings are long dinners under clear skies rather than busy resorts.

There is also variety. In one trip the group can climb a dune at sunrise, walk among rock engravings, kayak or sandboard at the coast and watch elephants drink at a floodlit waterhole. Different energy levels fit easily: the keen hikers climb Big Daddy while others take the shorter walk into Deadvlei.

Who is a women's trip to Namibia best for?

A women's trip to Namibia is best for groups of friends marking a birthday, mothers and daughters, sisters, walking or photography clubs, and women who have travelled solo but want company this time. It is less suited to anyone who dislikes long drives, because even a well-paced route has a few five-hour days on gravel.

If your group is torn between countries, compare it with our girls trip to Kenya, which trades Namibia's desert scenery for the Mara's big cats, or a girls trip to Rwanda built around gorillas and Lake Kivu.

A Route From the Dunes to Etosha

The classic route for a women's trip to Namibia runs in a loop from Windhoek: south-west to Sossusvlei, north to Swakopmund on the coast, inland to Damaraland and then to Etosha before returning to Windhoek. Ten days lets the group sleep two nights in each place and avoid the hardest driving days.

DaysBaseHighlights
1WindhoekArrivals on different flights, welcome dinner
2-3Sossusvlei (Sesriem area)Sunrise at Dune 45, walk into Deadvlei, Sesriem Canyon
4-5SwakopmundWalvis Bay lagoon, sandboarding or quad bikes, seafood dinners
6-7DamaralandTwyfelfontein rock engravings, desert elephant tracking
8-9Etosha National ParkGame drives, floodlit waterholes after dark
10WindhoekDrive back for evening flights

Sossusvlei and Deadvlei

Sossusvlei sits inside Namib-Naukluft Park, part of the Namib Sand Sea that UNESCO listed as a World Heritage Site in 2013. On a women's trip to Namibia, plan to be at the gate at dawn: the best light on Dune 45 and Deadvlei lasts only a couple of hours, and by late morning the clay pans are hot and glaring. Access rules for self-drivers on the final sandy stretch have changed more than once recently, which is one more reason to travel with a guide who handles it.

Damaraland and the desert elephants

Damaraland is rugged, rocky country where elephants have adapted to life in dry riverbeds such as the Huab and Ugab. Tracking them is a morning activity with a local guide, and sightings are likely but never promised. Nearby Twyfelfontein holds thousands of ancient rock engravings and is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Etosha's waterholes

Etosha is the wildlife finale of a women's trip to Namibia. Its huge salt pan draws elephant, giraffe, zebra, lion and black rhino to waterholes in the dry months, and several rest camps have floodlit waterholes where the group can sit with a drink after dinner. Our Etosha safari guide explains which camps sit best for game.

Short on time? The 5-day Namibia celebration safari covers Etosha and Sossusvlei for milestone groups, and the 3-day Namib Desert and Sossusvlei experience fits a long weekend before or after a work trip.

What Does a Women's Trip to Namibia Cost Per Person?

The cost of a women's trip to Namibia depends mostly on lodge level, group size and trip length. Visas and park fees are modest; lodges and the vehicle are the big variables, and both cost less per person as more women share. That is why a group of eight usually pays noticeably less each than a group of four.

Here are the fixed costs we build every quote around. They come from official Namibian and UK government sources and should be confirmed before you book, because Namibian park fees were raised in April 2026 and can change again.

Cost itemAmountNotes
Visa (UK passport)N$1,600 per adultOn arrival or e-visa; children 6 to 11 pay N$800, under 6 free (checked November 2026)
Park entry, foreign adultN$280N$140 entrance plus N$140 conservation fee, for Etosha, Namib-Naukluft, Skeleton Coast and others (checked November 2026)
Park entry, child 9 to 15N$180Children aged 8 and under enter free
Vehicle entry, up to 10 seatsN$60Higher for larger vehicles (N$150 for 11 to 25 seats)

The park fees above were set by a government notice that took effect on 1 April 2026. On a 10-day loop you pay park fees for each day inside Namib-Naukluft and Etosha, so budget for four to five park days per person.

How group pricing works

For every six paying travellers, the seventh place is free, which most organisers either take themselves or split across the group. Each woman can pay her own share directly, so nobody has to chase money. Single rooms carry a supplement at most lodges, so decide early who is happy to share a twin. Is Namibia Safe for Women Travelling Together?

Namibia is one of the calmer countries in southern Africa for travellers, and a group of women on a guided trip faces few problems. The UK government's advice points to street crime in Windhoek, theft from vehicles at fuel stations and accidents on gravel roads as the main risks, rather than anything in the parks.

The UK Foreign Office advice for Namibia recommends staying alert in Windhoek after dark, not hailing taxis on the street and never leaving a vehicle unattended at fuel stops. It also warns against driving outside towns at night because of wildlife and livestock on the roads.

Guided or self-drive for a women's trip to Namibia?

A guided women's trip to Namibia removes the two most stressful jobs: driving long gravel roads and dealing with a puncture far from help. The UK advice notes that accidents are common on gravel, and many rental policies exclude single-vehicle accidents. With a guide, the group can look out of the window instead of at the road. If your friends love driving, read our notes on guided versus self-drive Namibia safaris first.

When Should the Group Travel?

The best time for a women's trip to Namibia is May to October, the dry season. Rain is rare, roads are in good shape and Etosha's animals crowd the waterholes. June to August brings cold desert nights, while September and October are warmer and often the best months for wildlife at Etosha.

Average temperatures at Sossusvlei show how the desert shifts through the year. Pack layers whatever the month, since a cold dawn on the dunes can turn into a hot late morning.

MonthsDaytime highNight low
December to FebruaryAbout 29 to 30°CAbout 14 to 16°C
March to MayAbout 25 to 29°CAbout 10 to 15°C
June to AugustAbout 23°CAbout 7 to 8°C
September to NovemberAbout 25 to 28°CAbout 9 to 12°C

January to April brings afternoon storms inland, greener scenery and baby animals, but gravel roads can deteriorate and Etosha's game spreads out. Our month-by-month guide to the best time to visit Namibia covers each season in detail.

Where Are the Best Starry Nights?

The best starry nights are in the southern Namib around Sossusvlei, where the NamibRand Nature Reserve is a recognised International Dark Sky Reserve. Almost anywhere away from towns gives a sky full of stars, and dry-season nights are the clearest. Time the trip close to a new moon for the darkest skies.

Many desert lodges offer star beds, open-air decks or an evening talk with a telescope. For a women's trip to Namibia that wants a night under the sky without camping, ask for a lodge with a star bed and book it early, since these sell out. Our stargazing in Namibia guide explains moon phases and the best spots.

How Can the Group Mix Adventure With Downtime?

Swakopmund is the natural place on a women's trip to Namibia to rest and play. The coastal town has cafés, seafood restaurants and German colonial buildings, and it is the base for sandboarding, quad biking, kayaking on Walvis Bay lagoon and boat trips to see seals and dolphins. Two nights here give everyone a break.

Not every woman will want the same day, and a private trip makes that easy. Half the group can go sandboarding while the rest walk the seafront or book a massage. See our full list of Swakopmund adventure activities for timings and age limits.

Rooms, vehicles and the shared plan

Groups of up to seven on a women's trip to Namibia fit one 4x4 safari vehicle with a guide; larger parties use a bigger safari vehicle or two 4x4s that drive together. We send a rooming list template early, mark who needs a single and plan one or two special dinners. See all our group safaris for the types of trips we run.

Insider Tips

  • Book a year ahead: A dry-season women's trip to Namibia needs lodges at Sossusvlei and Etosha, which fill fast for groups
  • Agree the budget first: Set a lodge level everyone can afford before sharing any itinerary
  • Pack layers: Desert dawns can be cold even when afternoons are hot
  • Bring a buff and sunglasses: Wind and dust are common on the dunes and the coast
  • Keep cash for tips: Namibian dollars or South African rand both work, and small notes help
  • Pick a group chat lead: One person shares flight times and rooming so the guide has a single contact

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a women's trip to Namibia safe?

A women's trip to Namibia is a sensible choice for friends, especially with a guide. The main risks are street crime in Windhoek and accidents on gravel roads, not the parks. Stay alert in town after dark, use taxis booked by your lodge, hide bags in vehicles and avoid night driving.

How many days does a women's trip to Namibia need?

A women's trip to Namibia needs at least 7 days to see Sossusvlei and Etosha without rushing, and 10 to 12 days to add Swakopmund and the desert elephants of Damaraland. Distances are long and most roads are gravel, so fewer stops with two nights each make the trip far more relaxing for a group.

Do we need a visa for Namibia?

British passport holders need a visa for Namibia, available on arrival or as an e-visa for 1,600 Namibian dollars per adult (checked November 2026). Many other nationalities also need one. Passports must be valid for six months after arrival with three blank pages, so check your own rules before booking.

What is the best month for a women's trip to Namibia?

The best months for a women's trip to Namibia are May to October. Days are dry and comfortable, nights are cool, and Etosha's animals gather at waterholes as the bush dries out. June to August gives the coldest desert nights, while September and October are warmer and best for wildlife.

Can women in our group pay separately?

Yes. On Divulge Adventures group trips each traveller can pay her own share, and people can fly in on different flights. A deposit of 30 to 40 percent holds the booking and the balance is due two to four weeks before travel. For every six paying travellers, the seventh place is free.

Final Thoughts

A women's trip to Namibia rewards groups who keep it simple: a loop from Windhoek, two nights per stop, a guide at the wheel and the dry months of May to October. Settle the budget and rooming early, and the dunes, elephants and night skies take care of the rest.
